text:
devon: heads up — noticed during the canary rollout to dedicated v2 that the console quick-preview briefly shows saved-search results from other tenants when you rapidly toggle workspace selector. reproducer: switch to canary, hit preview, then quick-switch org twice.
jia: wait what — is that the authz header or the prefetch cache?
samir: i saw this once on staging too. suspect prefetch + session-affinity race on the proxy layer. :eyes:
devon: logs show: `GET /console/preview?org=org-123&canary=true` returns cache-hit and then another concurrent request `org=org-456` completes while UI still rendering the first payload
maya: can you paste the raw request ids and headers?
devon: sure — snippet:
```
X-Request-Id: req-9a3f
X-Org: org-123
X-Affinity: session-42
X-Cache-Key: preview:tenant:org-123:widget-7
```
then about 120ms later
```
X-Request-Id: req-9a40
X-Org: org-456
X-Affinity: session-42
X-Cache-Key: preview:tenant:org-456:widget-7
```
but UI rendered the first DOM from the second payload. looks like response ordering got swapped in the client because both responses shared same correlation id in the console layer.
jia: shared correlation id? where is that coming from — the edge? the client assigns it
samir: client assigns temporary `correlation_id` but we also overwrite it in the internal proxy with `X-Correlation` for routing telemetry. i think the console client code reuses a single promise map keyed by `widget-7` not by request id.
maya: so a UI-level scoping bug — not just backend cache. high severity though because it leaks tenant content into the DOM for brief moment.
devon: yep. the quick-preview component does `pending[cacheKey] = fetch(...)` and resolves into the same slot for subsequent requests. racing requests with different org params share cacheKey.
ops-bot: incident created: INC-2026-045 — quick-preview tenant bleed (canary). priority P1 until validated. Assigned to eng-platform.
developer oncall samir: i'll add a hotfix: change pending map key to include org id and canary flag, and send a guard that ignores stale responses based on `X-Request-Id`.
jia: also need telemetry to capture `preview_cache_key`, `org`, `request_id`, and `client_correlation` so we can track frequency and affected orgs. currently telemetry only logs cache key and latency.
samir: agree. quick patch deployed to staging now. rollout plan: canary to 5% for 30m, monitor `console.preview.misbind` metric.
maya: how do we detect misbind? we can add an assert in the client where response.org !== requested.org => emit `console.preview.misbind` with stack trace and dom snapshot id.
devon: good idea. add sampling 1% to avoid noise and PII.
deploy-bot: deploy queued: patch/sam/fix-preview-key pushed to canary pool (5%).
jia: long-term: we should avoid shared mutable maps keyed by non-unique values. suggest revamp of quick-preview to be request-id-first.
samir: noted — i'll file a tech debt ticket and add to eng-platform backlog: `TP-980 console: stabilize preview request routing + telemetry`.
maya: can we also add a safety fallback in the API: if `X-Org` header != payload.org then return 409 or strip body? defensive in case client bug slips through.
devon: API fallback seems risky for old clients. prefer client-side guard + telemetry + immediate patch.
ops-bot: INC-2026-045 updated: mitigation deployed to canary, metric `console.preview.misbind` added, P1 -> monitoring. Will escalate if >0.5% of preview requests in 30m.
samir: running load test on staging to simulate rapid org switches. will report in 20m.
jia: thanks all — huge :sparkles: for catching this before prod blast. follow-up doc: please drop short postmortem in #postmortems once resolved.
maya: +1. once stable, roll to 100% and prune the sampled dom snapshots after 7d.
devon: closing loop — i'll update the console PR with code comments and tests for the race condition.
